title: Putting the Cascade in CSS
prompt:
CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets — when more than one rule matches, the browser picks a winner. Specificity usually decides: id beats class beats type. When specificity is tied, the later rule wins.

Read a short overview on MDN: Handling conflicts.

The HTML is fixed. Write CSS so the computed text colors are:

  • Every p — start with color: blue (type selector)
  • Anything with class accent — color: green (class beats type)
  • The element with id hero — color: red (id beats class)
  • The paragraph with both early and late — make color: purple win using source order (same specificity; put the winning rule last)

After you Run, you should see blue, green, red, then purple text down the page.

html.starter:
Type selector only

Class beats type

Id beats class

Later rule wins when specificity ties

css.starter: /* id > class > type; if specificity ties, later wins */

tests.name: CSS validates
tests.feedback: Fix the CSS validation errors shown in the test details.

tests.name: First paragraph is blue (type)
tests.feedback: Use a type selector so every p starts with color: blue.

tests.name: .accent (not #hero) is green
tests.feedback: Add a .accent rule with color: green so it overrides the type selector.

tests.name: #hero is red
tests.feedback: Add a #hero rule with color: red so the id beats the class.

tests.name: .early.late ends up purple (order)
tests.feedback: Write .early and .late rules with the same specificity; put color: purple on the rule that comes last.
